rows.text: You're... actually {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}, right?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wh—What's going on? You're the Titan?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Oh my, the children of humanity... have passed the final trial at last.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I was wondering when you were planning to expose me. How did you know?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: The riddle-like trials, your distrustful-yet-sincere character, referring to {RUBY_B#Romance Titan}Mnestia{RUBY_E#} as your love, and...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The head of the Lotophagists is actually called Medea and not Calypso.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Since you knew from the start that I was not who I said I was, why did you wait until now to expose me?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Because I did not believe that {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} would walk this world in a human form. I was also afraid that the Titans were under the control of the black tide and would do us harm...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Also, "to make a claim, one must have evidence" — this is the precious knowledge that I acquired during my time at the Grove.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh... Excellent. To think we were able to gain a new chance at life in the midst of death — fate truly is a mysterious thing.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Well... Shouldn't you also tell us why you went through all the trouble of setting up these riddles?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Oh, the reason's quite simple.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I needed your help, and just like how you were wary of me, I had to ensure that you were not villains who were trying to get their hands on the Coreflame. I also had to ascertain that you were capable of dealing with the threat at hand.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Is this threat related to the black tide?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Indeed, and it's even more related to that lost item from before. Its owner is a quiet and paranoid hunter who seems to have been reborn from the black tide and is attacking along with it.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: As I could not do anything about them, I split my body up and escaped to avoid harm. I bided my time for a chance to seek assistance. Unfortunately, this was not a sustainable long-term plan.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Uh... What you mean is that you hid your own Coreflame?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Indeed, I split it into three. I hid one within the Golden Bough of Vows, and sealed another in the amber along with {RUBY_B#Romance Titan}Mnestia{RUBY_E#}'s remaining embers...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: As for the last one... It's currently in Anaxa's body, which is in dire need of repair.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: What? Do you mean that, you're using such a method...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hehe, after all, the scholars of the Grove have always been willing to lay down their lives to defend my Coreflame... As a respected god, it would be too embarrassing if I were to do nothing and simply watch the children of humanity give up their lives for me.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Especially that heretic named Anaxa. He did not even hesitate to tear his soul apart and use it to perform a miracle. He trapped all the creations of the black tide within the Grove so that they would not be able to harm others.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: His way of thinking was so out-of-the-ordinary that I felt it would be a waste for him to meet his demise in the black tide. And so, I decided to save his life.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Of course, this also meant that I was able to conceal myself and remain hidden... Well, that's also an "equivalent exchange," right?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Ah, I finally understand! So, you want us to lend you a hand in piecing your Coreflame back together! We'll also be able to save Anaxa that way!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: What a smart little bunny. This way, I'll be able to regain my true form, and you will be able to bring the Coreflame and your teacher back to Okhema...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...We'll also take down the black-robed swordmaster at the throne, together in one go.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: But... Cerces, aren't you the Reason Titan?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Heh... Even if I do not have the authority of Strife, I'm still a god.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I just need you to buy me some time against the warrior's blade... Once the Coreflame is re-formed, I'll be able to show my hand.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Excellent. Then, just continue climbing to reach my throne.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Turn the Golden Bough of Vows into firewood to reignite the Coreflame of Reason...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I'll leave it to you, children of humanity. May you be blessed with good fortune.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: It seems like... a fierce battle will be inevitable.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Don't worry! Trianne will protect everyone!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Ahead lies the Luminary Throne...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We're lucky that she has a good heart. I'm not one to venture out often, and while I have some savings, it takes a lot out of me to even talk to people, let alone haggle... Had it been another merchant, I would've been set back plenty.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And also... the battlefield that we're about to step onto.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ah, this...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Friends, can you feel it?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Aw, don't be shy. It's a cute nickname!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Mis—!
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wah! You can't say that! Lady Aglaea should always be "Lady Aglaea"!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Memmy, what's wrong?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: The memories here have a very intense smell...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...It's the scent of bulrush, sand, and the blazing sun.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Is this...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Professor Anaxa...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ha... My eyes can no longer see...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: No matter... All I have to do is to place this body at the core of the array...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: For the sake of Amphoreus... Die with me, Titan.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Ah...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} was right. He's indeed here.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Who is this black-robed guy...?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: This person is the source of the smell and the memory... No, he's basically the memory itself!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The burning paradise, the shattered sun, and...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Carnage. Death and destruction.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Everyone, brace yourself... This must be the hunter reborn from the black tide that {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} was talking about...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The black sword and cloak...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The owner of the piece of cloth... The north wind that sent over the deathly fog of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You're not... demigods.
Stand down. Or die.
Quick... run! It's just us... We won't be able to defeat them...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: T—Trianne will also protect everyone! Trianne is brave!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Only this time... may Death protect us!
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Phew... That was a close call. Thank goodness that we returned to Okhema unharmed.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Because Lady Aglaea... will probably be against it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh... Let me guess. That woman will not only prevent me from visiting the families of the deceased, but will also suppress any information about the Grove. She's always been that cold-hearted.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: My fellows at the Grove gave their lives defending the Coreflame and fighting the black tide alongside me. Their families... deserve to know the truth.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You intend to do it without her knowledge?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Do you really think that woman would treat me well even if I behaved and proved my loyalty? I wouldn't mind seeing a bit more anger on her face.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Are you going to stop me, Castorice?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...I will accompany you, but please understand that Lady Aglaea has her own considerations.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Heh, you truly have the makings of a fine scholar, putting yourself in other people's shoes like that.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let's go. I won't go overboard.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, after all these years, you and Lady Aglaea are still...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ugh... Little Cas, my head... It still hurts.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Neither of us is narrow-minded. You should know the root cause of our conflict.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Yes. He managed to protect {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces'{RUBY_E#} Coreflame at the cost of his life.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Mr. Fabio, the black tide... took Cynane and Artakama.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh... Just up and left me behind, that old man...
rows.speaker: Titus

rows.text: That is it. That's all the colleagues' families that I remember.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Good work, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer] and... Professor Anaxa.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please do not underestimate the threat the black tide poses.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lady Tribbie once traveled across thousands of cities in Amphoreus to repel the black tide, but even they have no recollection of this powerful enemy in all their journeys. Perhaps the fall of Strife has triggered even more terrifying events in unseen places...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's go. Take me to see Aglaea.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That might be the case if we only brushed the very tips of our fingers, but back then...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh... I wasn't expecting Amphoreus to temper the will of the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...May you never succumb to the dark side of Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...It seems you took things pretty hard.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Alright... I'll lead the way.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: After what happened at the Grove, there's sure to be unrest in the coming days. We should rest for now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...I'm afraid you'd probably find the task of organizing just as awful.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Miss Castorice, {M#Lord}{F#Lady} [Trailblazer], you're back.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Shortly after, in Okhema
Hello. We have an important matter to discuss with Lady Aglaea. May we trouble you to inform her of our presence?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Sorry... I know you... told me... not to open the gate...
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Please don't blame yourself, Lady Trianne. If it weren't for you, we would've already met our end at the Grove.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I feel awful... I need to go back... to get some rest...
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Lady Trianne, you haven't been well since you woke up... Are you sure you can make it back on your own?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: All this noise and commotion... Okhema hasn't changed a bit, has it?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Are you... Professor Anaxa?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: There's no need for doubt. The Titan no longer speaks. It is I, Anaxagoras of the Nousporists.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Indeed. You are the only one who would refer to yourself like that.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Professor, let me be frank: The mission Lady Aglaea entrusted us is to search for survivors, uncover the truth about the disaster at the Grove, and... retrieve the Coreflame of {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That does not surprise me. And now, I'm a survivor who witnessed the entirety of the disaster, as well as the defenseless bearer of a Coreflame.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Are you going to bring me to Aglaea to fulfill your duty?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That is indeed my duty, but I prefer not to present you to her as a captive or spoil of battle.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Fine. There's no need to make your life difficult. I'm not against meeting that woman.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But I have some things to take care of first. The families of some of my fellow Grove scholars live in the holy city. Before we meet Aglaea... I want to visit them.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: My apologies, Miss Castorice... Lady Aglaea has just informed me that she has no time to receive anyone at the moment.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Hmph, that's just great. She refuses to even see me.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Answer me this, friend. Did Aglaea order you to take me directly to prison?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Who... are you?
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Please don't jest... It's possible that she really is busy. Let's wait here a moment, and I'll try to contact her using the slate.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's fortunate we don't have to confront that woman while I'm hauling around this sick body. Castorice, and this friend I haven't gotten the chance to know — I'll take my leave for today.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That Titan made a myriad of adjustments on their own... My head still aches from that. I don't want to stay a second longer in this noisy city if I can.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Please be careful. Okhema isn't the Grove. This place...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Is covered by her golden threads, I know. That woman is extremely confident I won't escape her grasp.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Don't worry. As I said before, I'll mind my behavior.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], so many unexpected things happened on our journey to the Grove... We truly had no intention of putting you in danger, let alone face the black tide head on...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The black tide is not just an enemy of Okhema, but all of Amphoreus. Even back when the forces of Strife coveted the holy city, their warriors still undeniably halted the black tide outside Castrum Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} Coreflame now sits vacant and the black tide has returned... The Grove is an academic city with the best understanding of the black tide. It shouldn't have fallen so easily, and yet it was taken overnight, leaving the city in blood and tears, haunted by the spirits of departed heroes...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The trial of Strife is imminent. I pray Mydei will be able to steel his resolve soon...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lady Tribbie once traveled across thousands of cities in Amphoreus to repel the black tide, but even they have no recollection of this powerful enemy in all their journeys. Perhaps the fall of Strife has triggered even more terrifying events in unseen places...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: As for me... I detected a strong stench of death from that entity, but it wasn't because he had a connection with {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}... I'm afraid it's purely because he has sent countless others to their deaths.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Speaking of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}... {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], there is something else I wish to verify with you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You must have an idea of the... curse I bear by now. I was born as the Shadow of Death, a poison shunned by all living beings...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yet when you caught me in the Grove...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I'm curious why you weren't affected by my power, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: My apologies for the abrupt question. For all my life, I've always wondered: What is my connection to death? And why am I inextricably linked to {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], you must be tired after being on the move these past few days. Please set aside the tragedy at the Grove for now and rest for the day.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: (Castorice is right. I should get some rest. Mem is probably exhausted too. {F#She hasn't}{M#They haven't} made a peep.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I wonder how Dan Heng has been holding up these past few days.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Oh, he looks like he's been well.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Long time no see. I've heard about what happened from Phainon... You've been through a lot.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I was organizing logs. I also asked Hyacine for some research material from the Grove.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I discovered something interesting. Do you remember that Amphoreus's sky was sealed away by a Titan? {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila's{RUBY_E#} presence keeps this world isolated from the rest of the world beyond the sky.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It seems Hyacine's ancestors were the Sky Priests who worshipped {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}. Perhaps she can give us more clues to find a way back to the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Nothing out of the ordinary happened in the holy city in the past few days. I didn't have to talk to anyone either. It was kind of nice spending time alone.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You look tired. You should get some sleep before we set off tomorrow...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh, by the way, I heard some rumors... If you're going to wander around, I suggest avoiding the hot bath.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Alright.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It's time to head out with the west wind!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...The air's really hot and heavy. Has it always been like this?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Is someone... injured over there?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Oh! This many people...!?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Who in the world did this...?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: This is all you can do, huh? Pitiable "Deliverer."
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I heard it's the Kremnoan...
What's going on?
It's so hot...
This is really bad...
D-De!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Snowy! Even Snowy...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: The... culprit...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The culprit... is... Mydeimos...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Ugh!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: De! What did you do to everybody!?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Tch... It's just another duel where I claimed victory.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: D—Duel?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...As I expected.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: On the surface, these two are the mightiest warriors in the holy city, but they're still impulsive youths at heart...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Speak up, Mydei. Tell us exactly what kind of foolishness you and Phainon indulged in this time.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: (No. None of those sound right.)
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Some time ago...
(...Forget it.)
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Am I seeing things? Is the magnificent Deliverer finally deigning to step outside?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hmph.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "Hmph"...? What kind of response is that?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Nothing. I was just imitating your usual response.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I don't feel anything special from you... Have you passed the demigod trial?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The ritual hasn't reopened yet. In case you forgot — It hasn't been THAT long since I pulled you out of the trial.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I didn't forget.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Then, you're welcome.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "In twilight's last gleam, Okhema stands bold. Her walls sturdy, tales untold."
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "Dreaming of her fruitful gardens, pilgrims arrive from distant lands. Figs and olives, O so grand..."
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "...Yet little do they know, that they will step into flames, fuel to the fire, a burning brand."
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What are you playing at this time?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I just felt like reciting a few lines of poetry. Surely the crown prince of Kremnos knows how to appreciate poetry, right?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Kremnoans steer clear of such weak literature, but {RUBY_B#Garbaniphoro Grand Library}my library{RUBY_E#} doesn't lack collections of this kind —
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: These lines express the poet's yearning for their home, just as Okhema is distant from many people's homes.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...I know how to interpret poetry, {RUBY_B#scoundrel}HKS{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Ha... There's no point in pretending to be profound, my friend. Thank you for helping me out when I was in a tight spot, but it seems to me that you aren't prepared for the trial either.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't compare your situation with mine. My people are still relying on me. I can't ascend to godhood on my own without first resolving their issues.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: So... are you suggesting that you, the mighty Mydeimos and the heir to the throne of Kremnos, wish to defy the tradition that has endured among your people for millennia?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I'm still thinking about what I should do.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Never mind. It's probably not my place to offer you counsel.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: An idea does strike me, though...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Go ahead. Let's see what terrible ideas you've come up with this time.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Maybe we both need to relieve some stress. Come, Mydeimos! Let's recommence our previous competition...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This time... We'll see who can stay in the super hot bath for longer!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What? Are you chickening out?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The phrase "chickening out" does not exist in the Kremnoan language. I just find the situation absurd, that's all. All-knowing historian, are you not aware that we Kremnoans use boiling water from sword forging for our baths?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Looks like I'll have to teach you some royal etiquette today!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: And thus, an unprecedented sauna battle commences.
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: With unparalleled resolve, the two warriors' determination even alters the very hue of the steam. Flames intertwine with scalding vapor, reaching toward the heavens, shrouding the sky and the sun. The spectacle is so magnificent that none dare gaze upon it directly...
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: Since we can't see what's happening in the competition... Why don't I regale you with a tale of "kings" to pass the time?
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: Do you recall the legend of the "Gorgo Lion" mentioned by a certain veteran? The central figure — the "mane" character — was not the sole sovereign of that land. An oryx stood as its formidable rival.
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: Long before the dawn of Era Chrysea, the two beasts started their timeless battle on the plains of Tretos. The lion regarded the oryx as its food, while the oryx perceived the lion as a scornful, oppressive, and challenging barrier that it swore to topple with its antlers...
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: For tens of thousands of years, without respite, the two creatures thus continued their relentless pursuit and rivalry...
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: It fixated on its rival's fleeing form in the chase.
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: It set its sights on the other's neck, nearly within reach.
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: It was stuck in a corner.
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: It had nowhere to escape.
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: On the land of Amphoreus, some lives meet their end at dusk, some at dawn, and yet others... are fated to perish under the blistering sun at noon!
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: And at last, the most scorching moment of the day descended upon them! The formidable hand of fate heeded their call and arrived...
rows.speaker: Bath Sprite

rows.text: My lords, would you like me to reduce the temperature a little?
rows.speaker: Bath Attendant Daros

rows.text: Hmph...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Wh—What? Heh... You're chickening out already?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Get lost.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: A—Are you asking me to get lost? Or...
rows.speaker: Bath Attendant Daros

rows.text: Do... whatever... you want...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Please forgive my presumptuousness, my lords.
rows.speaker: Bath Attendant Daros

rows.text: ...What a spectacle of folly.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: This is what you get for daring to challenge a Kremnoan without understanding your own place.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: What I'm saying is... Your little game dragged down quite a few innocent souls alongside you.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...We will personally escort back home the customers left awestruck by our formidable presence.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This... This isn't fair...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You are wearing... way less... than I am...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Is this the latest trend now? Getting into the baths while dressed in full armor?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Don't look at me like that... It was he who challenged me. There is no word for "flee" in the Kremnoan language.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: After recovery, Phainon and Mydei escorted the fainted bathers away from the scene.
This time, Phainon narrowly triumphed with a stunning 27 to 25 victory in terms of the number of trips safely escorted.
Very well, let us bring this farce to a close, shall we? Warriors, it is time to get moving.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Alas... The Flame-Chase Journey is destined to be a lengthy one, replete with obstacles.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...But thanks to those two, all the gloom has vanished into thin air.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Though we just had quite the commotion, it's not every day that we find the Marmoreal Palace this serene. Shall we continue with our previous plans? Hyacine, would you care to join us?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Such an empty bath is indeed a rare sight...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I was looking forward to unwinding after work. I'd be delighted to accept your invitation, Lady Tribbie!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: How about we go to the biggest bath?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Let me check... The water temperature feels just perfect!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: So, how is the feeling of having the entire bath to yourselves?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Heehee, it's sooo good...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: But, Lady Tribbie... Aren't you going to soak in the bath with us?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: We will have to pass. After all, we've become children.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Please understand that she can no longer endure the heat of this pool due to the blessings of {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Oh...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Are you curious about us, Hyacine?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I am, but something tells me... that it might be better to change the topic?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Don't get all nervous. It's not something we can't discuss! The truth is... a long, long time ago... we were a mature adult just like Agy.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Then, because of reasons... we inherited {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}' divinity and gained the power of "Passage"...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: And in return, the price we had to pay was the splitting of our soul.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Each opening of the Century Gate intensifies the strain on Tribbie and the others. They are gradually regressing towards infancy, both in body and mind.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: We don't know what awaits us at the end, either. But anyway, that's why we have turned into children.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: In that case... when you opened that giant Century Gate above Okhema during the battle against {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Well, there's no way around it. We all know that the Flame-Chase Journey won't be a smooth ride.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Maybe... We can find a way to fix it. The primary research focus of Nousporists is the soul. We explore its depletion and methods to restore dispersed souls... As long as research continues, there might be a breakthrough that can help.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: We will do everything we can.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: So, your first reaction is in fact denial? You're indeed Anaxa's student.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I look forward to your good news, Hyacine.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Haha, now there's another reason to look forward to tomorrow...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...Ugh!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Lady Tribbie!? Wh—What's wrong?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Something's... off. It's that strong feeling again... Is it Trianne?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Wait, no... It's not Trianne this time...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...It's Trinnon! Trinnon is in danger...!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Ha, I win this round of escorting the bathers home.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How does one contender alone make a valid competition?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Offering a compliment or two wouldn't be the end of you, you know.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...{RUBY_B#scoundrel}HKS{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hai... What is that word? Is it your native tongue?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It means "hyena" — I'm likening you to a weak hyena. By the way, you emphasized the completely wrong syllable.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Though we've been acquainted for some time, I have... rarely heard you talk in the ancient tongue of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's because I'm not exactly a master at it, either. I can listen and read just fine, but when it comes to writing...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You can write?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You speak as if you don't have a brain.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Haha, that was in jest. I understand. After all, you... spent all your childhood wandering far from home.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Worry about yourself first, Deliverer. You also never mention your hometown apart from when you need to introduce yourself.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Well... It's because there isn't much to say. Aedes Elysiae is simply a tiny village that disappeared many years ago in the flames of war.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The only times I get to see it are in my dreams... and in...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: And in?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...And in the trial from the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I knew it.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Yes, I saw it all. Aedes Elysiae ablaze, with everyone — my family, friends, and my kin — lying in a sea of flames.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: A blood-red half-sun hung in the sky, just like on that day. And before my eyes, that murderer...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...killed Cyrene.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But I saw its form this time... A black cloak, an eerie mask, and a broken giant sword that carried an ominous aura...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I fought it in the trial. But even though I've been fighting, improving, and resolutely getting stronger all this time... I still couldn't defeat it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You were blinded by hatred and almost lost yourself in that trial.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That's right... And that's why I am truly thankful to you, Mydeimos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph, you've finally picked up some manners. Better late than never.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Then what about you, Mydei? What did you see in that trial? ...What do you fear?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There is no word for "fear" in the Kremnoan language.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...I'm getting the feeling that your language has no words at all.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But to answer your question, I saw Okhema in the trial, as well as...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...My old comrades.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hephaestion, Perdikkas, Leonnius, Ptolemy, and Peucesta... Ever since I returned from the Sea of Souls, these five had been by my side.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: We faced life and death together during our days in exile. Those ten years were arduous, yet filled with moments worth treasuring. Each night, we would gather by the campfire, savoring honey brews and singing our hearts out...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The wind in the wilds of Amphoreus smells like rust. Hephaestion would always tease me about adding goat milk to the honey brew, claiming I ruined the blood-red color of the drink. He had a scrawny figure, but was a relentless force on the battlefield, dispatching foes without so much as a blink.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Perdikkas was an expert in concocting medicines, delving into all those strange folk remedies. Leonnius was a swift runner and our most reliable messenger.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Ptolemy was a real bookworm, always spouting off in chapters and verses. When we left Kremnos, he made off with a stack of ancient tomes from the grand library — not like it mattered, since my family owns the library. And then there was Peucesta... Heh, he was the silent type, but a truly masterful musician...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...This is the first time I've heard you mention these five and their names.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They died on the battlefield before the Kremnoan Detachment managed to join Okhema.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Perdikkas was the first to go. He was shot in the stomach by a poisonous arrow from the people of Ladon in the second {RUBY_B#Fourth Month}Month of Cultivation{RUBY_E#}. In the end, his remedies mended all but himself.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "Mydeimos, do not mourn. I have achieved honor by bestowing a noble death upon the enemy..."
rows.speaker: Perdikkas

rows.text: You've heard about that outlander, right? {M#He}{F#She} has somehow made a connection with {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} and can completely replicate scenes from the past.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: We will ask for {M#his}{F#her} aid. Tomorrow, at the Abyss of Fate in the Temple of Janusopolis... we will show you everything from that distant memory, Krateros.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Leonnius died in the fifth winter. Aidonia's snowstorm lasted three full months. On the night of the fiercest storm, our foes launched their assault.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Aidonia... Is that the city Castorice used to live in?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yes. Those zealots were as fearless as Kremnoans in the face of death, but they lacked respect for honor.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: They cornered us in a bottomless swamp. Leonnius covered for our retreat, and they cut his legs off. He vanished into the mire of a foreign land, his body never to be recovered.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "This is perfect, Mydeimos... I can finally deliver the news of you ascending the throne to the nether realm..."
rows.speaker: Leonnius

rows.text: Twenty dusks later, we finally breached the walls of Aidonia and entertained the tyrant's plea for peace. However, the rebels refused to surrender and set up an ambush within the city...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Ptolemy and his cavalry met their end before they could even relish our triumph. Those obelisks that collapsed after being set on fire became their final resting place.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "Mydeimos, please tell my family: It was not cunning schemes that vanquished Ptolemy, but the immense weight of Amphoreus' entire history."
rows.speaker: Ptolemy

rows.text: Then, it was Peucesta. He lured the enemies into the city of Aenionus with his melodies, buying us invaluable time.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Our enemies, consumed by indignation when they discovered the trick, set the entire city and my soldiers on fire... His final words were recorded on a small clay tablet, fractured by the flames.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "Mydeimos, don the crown."
rows.speaker: Peucesta

rows.text: And at last, my most trusted friend, Hephaestion... He was supposed to stand by my side through it all, but a sudden relapse of his illness hit him on the eve of my duel against my father...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: He hid his condition from me, and by the time I returned victorious, he had but a breath left in him.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "A Kremnoan dying on a sickbed... I would be a laughingstock to everyone."
rows.speaker: Hephaestion

rows.text: "Hephaestion, my dear friend... Spare your strength. I'll go get a physician..."
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "No need... Even if Perdikkas were here, he couldn't stop destiny from taking me away."
rows.speaker: Hephaestion

rows.text: "No! None can take you away!"
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: "Mydeimos... {RUBY_B#Kremnoan}Our{RUBY_E#} king... Do not shed tears for me. It's not befitting of your status."
rows.speaker: Hephaestion

rows.text: "Farewell, my dear friend... You must... lead us back home..."
rows.speaker: Hephaestion

rows.text: ...Krateros! What's going on?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Ah, Mydeimos...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: It seems I was the one who exposed my vulnerabilities first... Heh.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Aglaea! I demand an explanation.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This man abducted Trinnon by force and forced her to bring him to the Vortex of Genesis.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: He then brazenly stepped into the trial of the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#}... And naturally, failed.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Is she telling the truth? Why did you do that?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Because I don't want to wait anymore. Your hesitation made me desperate.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: If you want to run away from your destiny to become king, then keep running. Someone will eventually stand up and fill in the gap left by Strife... Then they will lead our people home.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Age has blinded you, teacher!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Can't you see that I'm hesitating because of this very recklessness seared into your blood?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Krateros, do you truly believe you're worthy of entering the trial? To blaspheme against the prophecy?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Does the mission we Chrysos Heirs bear seem like child's play to you?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In the meantime...
Do you know how the Kremnoans see you, Aglaea?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: You're a hypocrite... and a megalomaniac! The prophecy of genesis and the Flame-Chase Journey are just excuses for you to seize power.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Silence, Krateros! Do you even know what you're saying?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Are you defending this woman, Mydeimos? How many wars did people start because of her and her so-called prophecy? How many cities fell in the past millennium, their people massacring each other?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Even if this so-called "genesis" really exists, will there be a place for the Kremnoans in that new world?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Are you done talking?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: By agreement between the Chrysos Heirs and the Council of Elders, those who trespass upon the Vortex of Genesis need not be tried by the Council. I am allowed to pass judgment alone.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Krateros, your actions are unforgivable. I hereby sentence you...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Agy, wait!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...We have a proposal. Someone has to resolve this conflict between the cities.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Lord Krateros did not use violence to harm us. We can sense that his anxiety stems from his concern for his people's future.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Please, Aglaea. Hear us out first.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I'm listening.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I'm sorry, Lord Krateros. We were so preoccupied with deciphering the fragments of prophecy that we neglected those of you not favored by its message... Your accusations were harsh but justified.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: We wish to earn your trust, and those of the Kremnoans. I think the best way to do that... is to take you to witness the source of the prophecy for yourself.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: ...How are you going to show me something that has no form?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...A fair proposal. I accept.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Until then, you will be stripped of your freedom. That is my one condition and I will brook no argument.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hmph, it is not the first time I've been made someone else's prisoner. Do as you please, "demigod."
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Teacher... why did you do this?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Forgive me, young master, but I just cannot wait any longer.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Ever since your father died, our people and I have been waiting for a day to revive Kremnos. We placed all of our hopes in you but never received an answer.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: This obsession for returning home has become a sickness for our people! Wise as you are, I refuse to believe that you can't see the truth...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You have a clear head, which is why you're also incomparably alone. A smart person can only choose to tangle himself with the mundane of this world.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: If you're truly capable of leading our people beyond this bloodstained fate, then prove it to me once more, Mydeimos.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Just as you did back then...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: A fierce fighter... I did not expect such heroism from a feeble Okheman.
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: Fulfill your duty as the victor, warrior, and tell me your name! I seek an honorable death from you!
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: Moments later...
As if you have any honor!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Listen closely! I am the leader of the Kremnoan Detachment — {RUBY_B#Mydei}Mydeimos{RUBY_E#}!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I'm here to finish you, father.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It is you... the beast spurned by all. So, you did defy death. The prophecy was true... You will bring an end to my Kremnoan dynasty.
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: Defy? You're wrong. Death fears me. It's the reason I have this body of steel.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: As for you, you already stand at death's door, father. You were the one who threw me into the Sea of Souls, the one who tried in vain to enslave a {RUBY_B#Nikador}Titan{RUBY_E#}, and the one who desecrated the body of a god...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Scoundrel}HKS{RUBY_E#}! You're a weak king! So weak that even the lowliest hyena is a more noble existence than you!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: And now, fate's reckoning is upon you!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Then swing your blade! Take my crown, coronate yourself with an old king's blood, and inherit it all... Become the new rightful king of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: No, I don't want the crown. Listen — If there's only one end for the kings of Kremnos, then the crown means nothing to me...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: All I want is your life! To avenge mother and my comrades!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But the walls of Kremnos will not fall with me. Do you truly think you can escape fate's grasp, my son?
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: Hahaha... You and I, we're both the same... We feast on strife and fear...
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: ...Now, kill me!
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: The son of Gorgo is destined to be crowned in blood!
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: Krateros...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: (A blackboard? And what is that drawing...?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (It doesn't ring a bell at all. Perhaps it's just a childhood doodle.)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (It's packed full... Mama must have left all of these for me.)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (All the words are blurred out... Could it be that my memory is fading?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (I used to sit here and listen to Mama tell stories...)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (Oh, how I wish to see you again... Mama.)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Now, Tribios, set them on this music box and let them compose a melody for our song.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: M—Music box? What's that?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Sweetheart, are you still groggy from your nap? You invented it!
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: I... invented it? What does it do?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Oh, my lovely Tribbie, you're usually so bright! What's gotten into you today?
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Well, you might as well see for yourself. Put your good friends on it and see the wonders it can do.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: (Put the dolls on...)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: What's this...!?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Use the spindle to connect everyone!
Bad chest, you can't lock me away!
Learning can change your destiny!
Moments later, in Tribbie's room...
Momma, Momma! I had a dream last night.
Oh? Now, what did you dream about, my darling Tribios?
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: I had a dream that I turned into many mes! Then we made the moon into a ship and made the stars into our sails! Then we floated on the ocean and let the wind blow us in any direction it wanted!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Well that sounds like a lovely dream.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Yeah! The ocean and the sky were really, really dark, but there were so many of me that I wasn't scared at all. Because we'd all sing together!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: The ocean wind blew us onto an island where the wind tasted like flowers. There were bleating sheep and chirping birds inviting us to be their guests. There were so many animals on the island, but none of them ever fought!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}' Holy Maidens can receive guidance from the god of passages. Perhaps what you saw in your dream is a divine land somewhere in Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Y—You think so?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: What's wrong, Tribios? You look unhappy.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Because... on that same island, I saw a dark mountain on the other side of the ocean. And it was very, very tall.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: The mountain looked alive, and it kept getting closer to the island. Then I realized that it wasn't a mountain, but a very, very tall wave made of water... When the wave smashed against the island, it looked like it was going to eat the island up. The small animals tried to chase it away, but they couldn't stop it...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Then there was a "bang!" and I woke up.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Hm... A dark wave...
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Momma, does something that scary exist in real life?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Yes... Unfortunately, it does exist in Amphoreus, but it's very far away from our temple.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: We call it the "black tide," though it has nothing to do with water. It has no shape or form, but it can swallow up animals, humans, and even Titans... turning them all into monsters.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Ooh... The black tide is a baddie! I don't want everyone to turn into its food. Can't we chase it away?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Of course, my dear. You only need to behave well and listen to what the adults tell you, study all the knowledge and etiquette you need, then grow up and become a proper Holy Maiden...
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: The divine {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#} will then give you guidance and help you light the way for the people.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Wow! I'm gonna eat a lot and study a lot and become a Holy Maiden!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: But, Momma, you said the black tide can swallow up Titans too. What do we do if even {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#} is eaten?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: If that happens... then the Holy Maiden will have to be the one to guide people on the right path. After all, we are the human avatars of the god of passages, yeah?
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Yeah!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Hehe. But one person alone is not enough. Once you're older, you'll make a lot of friends. You must do your best to unite them because that's also our duty as priests.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Friends? Are they also like me and Momma, with pretty red hair?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: They might not, but they'll certainly be just as smart and kind as you.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: (Mama...)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (Am I... dreaming?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Don't be silly, dear. Of course you're not dreaming. I've always been by your side.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: (What...)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Now be a good girl and call {RUBY_B#doll}your friends{RUBY_E#} over too...
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Let's play hide-and-seek just like we used to, okay? My Tribios is the smartest girl. I'm sure you remember where everyone is hiding.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: (The voice... sounds so far away.)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I don't... remember... Who am I looking for?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Your friends who will chase the black tide away alongside you, of course.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: There will be an amazing captain on that big ship. She's cheerful, optimistic, bold, and cautious. She'll be able to get everyone together.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Wow, that's amazing! Can I be the captain?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Of course you can! But you'll find someone else who's better for the job, my dear.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: I think that person lives in a beautiful temple that sits atop a hillside covered in golden fig trees.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: There's a noble girl there who's very smart but also very delicate.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Just like Momma...?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Perhaps. But before we find the captain, the ship also needs someone who can navigate it. Who could that be?
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Mmm... Let me think...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: I know! She's... "Tribbie"!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: (I named this doll... after myself?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (I don't remember at all... Is this a dream, or something that happened in the past?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (Huh? Why is this doll inside a chest...?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (It's holding a... sword? Why...)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Many years later, many brave warriors will board this ship. They are skilled combatants who fear no danger.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Ooh... I can learn how to fight too and protect everybody!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Silly girl, you're Janusopolis' Holy Maiden. It's not your duty to fight. There will be many others to protect you.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Alright, then where will they come from?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: I believe one warrior hails from a lovely village where bulrushes flourish, while another comes from a magnificent royal city. Though each has their own troubles, both are ready to lend their strength for the ship's long voyage.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: In that case, let "Trianne" fight by their side!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: This way, they'll always stay on course!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: (How could I have known the name "Trianne" back then?)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: (Was it just a coincidence, or...)
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: When navigating at sea, you need to know both astronomy and geography.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Ugh... isn't {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}' knowledge enough?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Oh, sweetie. The ocean isn't like the land. It's easy to get lost. That's why it's important to learn to recognize the miracle of {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Alright! Even though my brain is already super-duper smart, I'll still try my very best!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} also favors children who try their best. They will send a wise scholar as everyone's teacher to help you reach your dreams.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: I wanna be a teacher too! Oh, wait, I'm super-duper smart! So I wanna be the teacher's teacher!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Why not? But if you're going to be a teacher, you might need to tone down that hyper energy of yours.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Then... "Trinnon" can do it! She's well-behaved and would make a great teacher.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: (Mama and the others always said I had a great memory...)

rows.text: Over here! Follow Trianne—
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We need to go after that black-robed swordmaster.
Trianne... I have a bad feeling about this.
Tribbie! Trinnon! Look what I found! Is this the "safari"?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Coming! We'll take a look...

rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: What do you mean?

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...We can choose how our branches will perish in a way that is most beneficial to the Flame-Chase Journey.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Compared with saying farewell to one person... watching many fade away before me is even more sorrowful.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: What? Where did that come from...?

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Heh, while my emotions might be fading, those memories are still as vivid as ever, teacher.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Please, let me do it. What would you like to eat?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It's fine. Leave it to us. You should rest for now. It won't take long, and we will call you once it's done.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...In that case, thank you.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Then... See you tomorrow, Agy!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Monster in the black cloak, so scary. Everyone, in danger... Nightmare, can't forget.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Don't be scared... There are no bad guys here. Didn't you save everyone with the Century Gate, Trianne?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Trianne threw it away. Far, far away. It's never coming back.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: We got back safe from the Grove because of you, Trianne. You're the reason the Flame-Chase Journey can continue.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Sorry, Trianne feels... a bit dizzy. Why are we here again?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: For the same thing, of course. Remember? Tomorrow, we will reveal the prophecy's past to everyone.

rows.text: But first, we need to restore the memories that have been blurred by the fragmentation. We hope to present the full truth to everyone, without hiding anything.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Since {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#} caused the fragmentation, we can only turn to another Titan, {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}, for help.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Also... remember to get breakfast ready for Agy before the {RUBY_B#Morning}Lucid Hour{RUBY_E#} tomorrow!

rows.text: Ah, yes! Trianne remembers now!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Oh, on that note... we had better prepare some "saffron" before we meet with the Titan.

rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Yes. It's also a symbol of Janusopolis. If we are to replicate memories, we need to use something that has experienced those days...

rows.text: And when we first met Agy, we added that to the porridge we made for her, and she really loved it!

rows.text: I see! It's like killing three birds with one stone!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: But... it all depends on whether {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} is willing to help us.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: This... could be a problem.

rows.text: After all, it was us who took the Coreflame from {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}... From Oronyx's kin.

rows.text: We will have to give it a try. If there is truly no other way...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...In our current state, we probably can't do anything to them. We'll cross that bridge when we get there...

rows.text: Leave it to Trianne. Trianne knows how to play cute!

rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This is the most plausible possibility. First, it has a vessel that can hold Coreflames. Second, I'm one of its targets.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The second premise is even more explicit. When it was engaged in fierce battle with many of us and was heavily distracted, it remained consistently focused on me — or rather, on the Titan {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} inside me.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh, so it's plundering the flames...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not necessarily. Let's call that person the "Flame Reaver" for now. If my presumption holds, that person has three targets.

rows.text: The first target is me. The second target is {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}, who hasn't yet fallen. And the third is Okhema and the Vortex of Genesis, where the Coreflames are housed.

rows.text: But I suspect Okhema won't be their first target. {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame is guarded by the Council of Elders' arcane power, and {RUBY_B#Ocean Titan}Phagousa's{RUBY_E#} water curtain should be able to block out any external perceptions.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What about {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}? Their Coreflames are yet to be restored...
rows.speaker: Phainon
