rows.text: I just have to throw that black-cloaked guy into the past, and lock them there, right? With the memory fragments, I can open a door no problem. As for the rest...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Yes. I'm sure everyone remembers the astonishing miracle [Trailblazer] performed with {M#his}{F#her} companion during the battle with {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} and how they awakened Castrum Kremnos' past.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well, let's just say that [Trailblazer] and I can do anything as long as we're together!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Such enthusiasm. I'm glad to see you're confident.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: By the way, the Council of Elders declared a state of emergency when Tribbie went missing. Caenis and her following have heard tell of the incident at the Grove and are galvanizing support in secret. I fear she'll make her move before the next assembly of the citizens.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: What are they plotting...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: That short-sighted politician likely believes the Chrysos Heirs have outlived their usefulness and is making preparations for her next step. That ugly side of humanity is something we'll have to deal with eventually.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...But that's a problem for another day. I've sent Castorice ahead to the Council with a message. She should be able to keep the situation under control for the time being.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Phainon, it is my hope that we can come to an understanding on this: We must take down the Flame Reaver in one go and retrieve the Coreflame, and in doing so, grant ourselves an advantage against the Council of Elders.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Of course. You may count on me to lead the charge.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I apologize for tasking you to spearhead the plan once again, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], but Okhema is currently beset by enemies from within and without.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The situation brooks no delay, and we have precious little time to confer and discuss the plan with you... That being said, you are the key to our success, and I shall respect any decision you make.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: We are grateful to you for your aid, and to the rest of you as well. Now, let us be off to begin the hunt.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: May {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} sharpen our gaze and grant us victory over the enemy.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You mean Mydei? He's dealing with a different problem.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry. That man would never miss out on this fight.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Farewell, my dear friend. You must... lead us back home...
rows.speaker: Hephaestion

rows.text: As for whether we can take back the Coreflame... that will be up to Anaxa's capabilities.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Based on what I know of him, he can do it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But the Flame Reaver will have to step over my dead body if they wish to do you harm.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You and I, we're both the same... We feast on strife and fear...
rows.speaker: Old King Eurypon

rows.text: If you're truly capable of leading our people beyond this bloodstained fate, then prove it to me once more, Mydeimos.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: I knew you'd be here.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I heard you're about to set off on an expedition.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That's right. It's going to be a tough battle, and our destination is... turns out to be Castrum Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Is that why you're here? To pray to the dead {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: No, just the opposite. I'm here to tell you...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You can entrust the front line to us this time. You can't afford to lose your upcoming battle either.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Have you heard the story of Geocles the Mountainbreaker?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Sounds like you've spoken with Chartonus. That's the name of the legendary Mountain Dweller, right?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's have a chat before we go our separate ways.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Chartonus told me that back in ancient times, the Mountain Dwellers lived in seclusion. They spent their days quarrying and gathering, living a simple and peaceful life away from strife.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But Geocles was different. He resisted their traditional way of life, yearning for the world beyond the mountain. Their safe but humdrum culture was like fetters around him.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: He sounds a lot like you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yes, that is why he, too, faced the same dilemma as I do. One day, during one of Geocles' many ventures beyond the mountain, he spied a battalion of Ladonians stationed at the foot of the mountain.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The Ladonians were at war with their archenemies, the Campanians, and they used the mountain as a base to carry out guerrilla warfare operations. When Geocles, who had taught himself the common tongue, approached a soldier, he learned a shocking piece of news:
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Alright, I suppose that's putting it lightly. Don't worry, you'll figure out the intricacies of these relationships sooner or later.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The Ladonians were planning to plant mines and explosives all over the mountain, and then lure their enemies within. With danger lurking with every step, the Mountain Dwellers' homes were no longer safe. Geocles quickly returned to his village to bring the news to his people, but...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Let me guess: They refused change and chose to put up with the situation instead?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...That's right. The Mountain Dwellers were fearful of even the smallest change to their lifestyle, let alone leaving their home. Despite the imminent war, the elders would rather negotiate for peace instead of leaving the mountains. This made Geocles both angry and sad.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But he didn't give up. If you were in his shoes, what would you have done?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Lead my people on a resistance, perhaps? I'm not sure. I can't think of a solution that would make everyone happy.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "A solution that would make everyone happy," huh... That's how naive we are. Well, let me tell you what Geocles did.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: He took the Mountain Dwellers' store of gemstones and traded them with the Ladonians for a massive amount of gunpowder — but he didn't do this to fight the Campanians. Under the cover of night, he set ablaze the forests surrounding the settlement, forcing his people to flee the mountain.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That great fire marked the beginning of Mountain Dweller history. Since then, their people became part of civilization, and giants became a common sight in the holy city. Meanwhile, that mountain they once lived in has turned into little more than foam inside the black tide.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But leaving their homeland also brought many Mountain Dwellers misfortune. They —
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They were hunted by Kremnoans or enslaved. Indeed, that is undeniably also part of their history.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But that is Geocles for you. The merits of his actions — or the lack thereof — have been scrutinized by many, but historians nevertheless hail him as the Mountainbreaker. Why do you think that is?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It's simply because he took action and enacted change with his own hands. He didn't try to make everyone understand him, nor did he even waste time trying to make everyone happy.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: He started a great fire and burned the shackles of tradition to ashes, and then... forced everyone to march toward the coming of a new era.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...You've made up your mind, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I'll be leaving Okhema soon to fight the great darkness of this world... and to shoulder {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} destiny.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: So, listen well: If there comes a day when we meet again on the battlefield, and I stand opposed to the flame-chase...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Remember to stab your sword into my back through my tenth thoracic vertebra. That's my weak spot, and the only way to kill me.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You have my word.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Go now. Your battlefield calls. Send that flame-thieving hyena to their death.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But if you find yourselves with no other recourse, then pray to that blade in the sky...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...And loudly call out the name of the new god.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That's the sound of an all-out war. Not the kind of ruckus Professor Anaxa can raise on his own.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's hurry. The battlefield is just ahead.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No way... A Kremnoan?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I didn't think she'd manage to send the Kremnoans to assist. Brave warrior, what's the situation on the front line?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...An Okheman? Why are you here...?
rows.speaker: Exhausted Kremnoan

rows.text: What...? Didn't Aglaea tell you? We have been instructed to assist you in trapping the Flame Reaver.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Vortex of Genesis, Okhema
Aglaea... That vile tyrant! I spit on her name!
rows.speaker: Exhausted Kremnoan

rows.text: Our king... will be back soon... He'll be able to... deal with you... and that black-robed...
rows.speaker: Exhausted Kremnoan

rows.text: ...The Kremnoans really are just like their king.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Rest in peace. May your glory last forever.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We're almost there...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But remember what Mydei said before? "Cast aside all distractions once you're on the battlefield"...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's go, partner! Today, destiny shall stand with us!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Look, the warriors have returned!
rows.speaker: Chattering Citizens

rows.text: But... are the rumors true? Has {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} fallen?
rows.speaker: Chattering Citizens

rows.text: It's as the Council of Elders said. We face a dangerous threat, yet the Chrysos Heirs are only inciting more chaos. They don't care about the people's safety...
rows.speaker: Chattering Citizens

rows.text: They really gave the Coreflame of "Strife" to a Kremnoan at the end...
rows.speaker: Chattering Citizens

rows.text: What a noisy crowd...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This... doesn't feel right.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's probably because {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} is gone...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} was a generous Titan in the eyes of the people. They graced us with miracles, allowing humanity to reap many a convenience from the past...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: What they don't know is that the Titan didn't do all of that of its own volition.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Regardless, the Titan has fallen, and we must surrender {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Heh... a meeting with that woman again so soon? I just can't catch a break.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Professor Anaxa, why don't you... find someplace to rest first?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Matters that require Aglaea's attention are piling up. You two meeting again will — forgive my honesty — only distract her.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Just... try to stay on your best behavior, if you know what I mean.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's not up to me, I'm afraid. I've been trapped in her prison the moment I set foot in this holy city. The price of having a Titan living in my head, I suppose.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Don't worry. I don't want trouble either.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I'm sure you don't need my help handling {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame, so I'll be off. I have some personal matters to attend to.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It somehow feels like De has closed himself off even more after he completed his trial.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Yeah. A lot has happened in the past few days...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You've been lost in thought for a while now too, Tribbie. Did Trinnon bring news?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yes... She has found Trianne.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...She was at the bottom of the valley outside the temple. But... that's where the good news ends.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...I'm sorry.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's alright. They also found someone else besides Trianne.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: He was no better than a corpse when Trinnon and Hyacine arrived. He had suffered more cuts than could be counted and leaped off a cliff from a great height, all to free Trianne's body from the clutches of the black-robed swordmaster.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: What a brave soul. Do we know who he is?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yes...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: It's Krateros.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...Stop!
Heh.
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: If you want this girl dead, you'll have to kill me first.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: How ludicrous... Your body, made of flesh and blood as it is, will not survive more than a single strike from me.
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: "Valorous Death Before Glorious Return." As a Kremnoan, I know not the fear of death.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: She's lost her divinity. I have no interest in an empty shell.
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Not long ago...
But answer me this, child of Strife. Why do you raise your shield for her?
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Hmph...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: As the leader of the Godshield Brigade's elite, I protected the king against the black tide with this very shield. And I've done this over and over, hundreds and thousands of times...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: A pathetic killer like you could never understand the weight it bears.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Pity.
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Then crumble like rusted iron.
rows.speaker: Flame Reaver

rows.text: Good! Supreme glory shall be mine as I indulge in the libations and incense offered by my descendants!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Come, let us fight! For Kremnos! For my king!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...For Amphoreus!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: We foresaw this cruel parting a thousand years ago. Today is but a reminder of that bitter taste.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But Lady Aglaea, I don't understand... It wasn't life itself that Lady Trianne lost...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Why does she look like she really turned into a doll? I... I don't understand...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Don't be sad, Hyacine. Trianne has used up her borrowed time from {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}, that's all.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Her spirit is now riding the west wind, flying ahead to a world free of sorrow.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: If a world like that truly exists...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Does that mean everyone from the Grove is there too?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: It exists, Hyacine. Do you not remember? The prophecy that guides the Chrysos Heirs is the voice of Kephale before it fell silent.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It loves all of its creations dearly, and would never bear to lead us astray with lies.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: What about the Kremnoan veteran? How is he doing?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The Twilight Courtyard has done all we can. Even so, we've only managed to keep him from breathing his last.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I had to use the Sky Priests' techniques to help him walk again, but if light ever disappears from Okhema for good... No, let's hope that never happens.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: This is already nothing short of miraculous. When we found Krateros, he was no better than a corpse.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The {RUBY_B#Dusk}Parting Hour{RUBY_E#} is upon us, yet the golden thread runs slack. The heroes have returned with their spoils.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Everyone, please take this opportunity to rest and prepare for what awaits us.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It's incredible to think that we returned {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame not so long ago... It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say that [Trailblazer] and your friend's arrival has melted the glaciers of history.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You could say this is the true face of history. It slumbered for a thousand years, only to awaken for this one moment. Alas, now is not the time for a study of history.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I do not see Anaxa around. Was this under your instructions, Phainon?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Yes. It just seems much more efficient than letting you two go at it endlessly.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: A rash decision. After all, he still bears a Coreflame with him.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I do concur with your assessment of efficiency, though. Now, let us table the issue concerning him for the moment. The more urgent matter is the Coreflame of {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Nikador is with us!
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier A

rows.text: We won't bring dishonor to the king!
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier B

rows.text: I can still... fight...
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier A

rows.text: You must become king...
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier B

rows.text: That sound... It pierces my ears...
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier C

rows.text: I can't see...
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier D

rows.text: For Kremnos! For the king!
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier C

rows.text: Glory to the Godshield Brigade!
rows.speaker: Kremnoan Soldier D

rows.text: The Chrysos Heirs had initially crafted a plan regarding the order to return the Coreflames. For Titans like Oronyx and {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}, who harbor no intentions of harming humanity, our strategy entailed assuming their divinity only at the very end.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But this unforeseen turn of events has thrown everything into disarray.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: If we don't return the Coreflames to the Vortex of Genesis and we leave the Titans' divine positions vacant... we can't even begin to imagine the disaster that would follow!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: But the most pressing issue at hand... is that we haven't found the Chrysos Heir capable of bearing {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s divinity.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Phainon, Castorice, Mydei, and Hyacine... Tribbie and I devoted a millennium scouring the world, only to find these few people.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Only a chosen few possess the capacity to assume divinity, the elite among the Chrysos Heirs. We would never hastily extend our invitation without first verifying their potential to bear such power.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Yet we cannot compel anyone into divinity, as it would be no different from sentencing them to the gallows.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Truly a dilemma...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yeah...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: A hoarse curse lodged in his throat, refusing to escape. Moments later, he convulsed, his head drooping as his spirit departed his body, drifting towards the abode of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}.
Well...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: How about letting [Trailblazer] give it a try?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Once we take back the Coreflame, {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}' passage will open. When that happens, you must evacuate immediately. Don't stay behind.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: The rest... will be up to how well we work together.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I'm serious! You're special to Amphoreus, and we all know that. Now, about {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Isn't the one who projected me into this world and granted me this body... that {RUBY_B#Time Titan, Oronyx}baby Titan even more capricious than a child{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: There are some people to meet with before I leave.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Let's go.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The King of Kremnos, without the signet ring... But looking more like a king now.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: I'm no longer the "king," Grand Craftsman.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Matters not, the title. Surpassed all former kings, your achievements have.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: I will honor your trust and liberate the world from the clutches of fear.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Nevertheless, I must request that you continue to watch over Phainon, Chartonus. I have a feeling that his fate... will weigh heavier than all of ours combined.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Keep Phainon in mind, I will. Return to your home, brave king.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: Together with everyone, I shall remain here. That thunder... from Castrum Kremnos, we wait to hear.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: And what is next, Mydeimos...?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...Where will you be headed now?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Meanwhile, somewhere in Marmoreal Palace
It's been a while, "Guardian."
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Have a safe journey.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: We salute you!
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: Farewell, Guardian!
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: You're our hope!
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Farewell, Mydeimos!
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: May triumph always be yours, King of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: I think I see... more than just the Kremnoans here.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You're now the Guardian of Amphoreus, after all.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I'm thinking... Maybe it's about time the god of "Strife" gets a new name.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How about the god of "Solidarity"? Or... "Preservation"? Dan Heng mentioned that one to me.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I recommend that you steer clear of any situation that calls for naming things.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hah... I suppose "Strife" still fits you better.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: May triumph always be yours.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: We salute you.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: We dedicate our lives to following you.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Enlighten us with your guidance.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: You will forever be our king.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: Farewell... Savior of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Return home on our behalf, Guardian!
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: May glory be with you.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Please fend off the black tide for us, Guardian...
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: We salute the Guardian of Amphoreus!
rows.speaker: Demetri

rows.text: I'm all ears, Lord Mydei. I'll make sure to convey every single word.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: May glory be with you.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: We salute you.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: May triumph always be yours.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: May glory be with you.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: Enlighten us with your guidance.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: You will forever be our king.
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: We dedicate our lives to following you.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Are you thinking about... saying something inspiring?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Are you drafting... a sentimental farewell speech?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Are you going to say something insane again, Trailblazer?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Looks pretty good. What do you think, Mydei?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hmph, well... It feels peculiar, I suppose? I'm not talking about your photographic skills. It's just that I rarely take photos...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But this one... It's pretty good.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I never fail to impress.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm glad you like it. Make sure not to leave any regrets behind.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...I wish the same for you during your time in Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Is Lady Tribios not here...?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Lord Mydei!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Hyacine?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: So you are the physician Krateros spoke of. It's no wonder then that he was pulled back from the brink of death. You have my gratitude.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Heh... I can take that as a compliment, right?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I've heard about what happened at the Grove. I am deeply sorry for your loss.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...I've heard far too much about death and grief recently. To quote Lady Tribbie, we should all focus on tomorrow, shouldn't we?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: That's a valid point... You have always been the most optimistic one among us.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Well, I must say, it feels quite incredible... to see a new demigod standing right before me.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: You should prepare yourself as well.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Humanity has already taken hold of "Strife," and one day, they will also reach the "Sky."
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Do you really believe I can do it? Even my ancestor, that hero of legends, couldn't conquer the Coreflame of {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Given your good rapport with the demigods, you should know that the path to assuming divinity is never limited to swords and spears.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You've always been so perceptive, Lord Mydei. Rest assured. If fate has truly selected me, I will be ready.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Right. You are here looking for Lady Tribbie and Lady Trinnon, no? They're not around at the moment. Is there a message you'd like me to pass on to them?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: No need. I have already bid farewell to Aglaea. Meeting with the oracle is simply a matter of courtesy.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You've bid... farewell?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I'm heading back to Castrum Kremnos to fight against the black tide. In all likelihood, I will never again return to Okhema.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Oh...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: On second thought, there is something that I'd like you to help me convey to them.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Tell them that there is no longer a need to send scouts behind enemy lines. With a single message, the Lance of Fury will target anyone who dares oppose Okhema.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hmph, I should've known you were the mastermind behind this.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hey, don't go pointing fingers without cause. I swear I'm innocent this time.

rows.text: See those kids over there? They're the ones who brought everyone together.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...I admit, that took me by surprise.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Were you seriously just going to sneak off without a word with me?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well, I was actually on my way to bid farewell to you, but ended up running into this.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Oh... That's quite an honor, I suppose.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We better not leave them waiting too long, don't you think?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The road to Castrum Kremnos from here is long.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The prince is here. Run!

rows.speaker: Marsyas

rows.text: What's going on?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I see the Reaper has forsaken you, too, teacher.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hmph, it simply put my life in the hands of the Twilight Courtyard.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: That priest girl's medical talents are truly exceptional... She might be far from the ordinary girl we envisioned.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: But this isn't about me, Mydeimos. I saw it... You've finally decided to embrace your own fate.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: The power of Strife is stirring a tempest within me as we speak... My bones have turned into steel, and my blood is seething and ablaze. Past rulers of Kremnos could only aspire to this might, yet I have merged with it.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I've made history, and henceforth, divinity and kingship shall coexist as one.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Indeed. You've realized the aspirations of every former king of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: And now, you can at last bring our people home and reforge the glory of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...Unfortunately, I harbor no such desire.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Wha—What do you mean by that?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Over two millennia past, devotees of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s might banded together beneath their feet and erected a city of their own. Ever since then, Kremnoans have served as the blades wielded by the god of war, following the Titan's path in its conquest.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Yet, gazing upon our history through the lens of my newfound divinity, I now see it with unprecedented clarity.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This history is sheer absurdity and inferiority. People surged onto the battlefield like ants, plundering and slaying for their own greed, only to be trampled upon... like ants.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The city and the beliefs that Kremnoans hold so dearly, alongside the supposed tradition... are mere anthills that can be crushed with a single touch in the eyes of the Titan.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You...!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Are you trying to strip Kremnoans of the pride we've amassed over thousands of years with mere words!?
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: ...That pride holds little significance, Krateros. Now that I've assumed the divinity of Strife, my next step...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Will be to renounce the title of "King."
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...No! NO!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Convey my message to every Kremnoan — this is an order.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Do not do this, Mydeimos...
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: I beg you...!
rows.speaker: Krateros

rows.text: Our history commenced in Year 2506 of the Light Calendar and concluded in Year 4931. I, Mydeimos, last King of Castrum Kremnos, son of Gorgo, do hereby proclaim...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The Kremnoan dynasty comes to an official close today.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Alright... It's about time for us to part ways.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Any final goodbyes you want to share? This might be your last chance.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Why so quiet? I thought divinity would wash away some of your sentiments.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Do you truly feel as carefree as you seem? Or... is this just a facade you wear?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...You know what, you sound just like Aglaea at this moment.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But you're not off the mark... I just thought putting on a nonchalant front for this occasion might help us preserve some dignity.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I can see through your deception even without the power of mind-reading.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Am I really that terrible at controlling my facial expressions?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well, with that said... thank you for aiding me in defeating my archenemy, Mydeimos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No need to thank me.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This triumph brings no delight, nor does it signify closure — you understand that more than me.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Indeed. In the end, I still haven't unraveled the mystery behind that black-robed swordmaster, and I can't even ascertain their demise.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Maybe I've never managed to cut off my destiny.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But that matters not. Pain may be cured, but scars remain, and they should not be effaced. Even with the divine might of {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}, you cannot stop the past from leaving its marks in our blind spots.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Can you genuinely let go of everything as soon as that swordmaster is dead? That's impossible. Revenge is merely an obligation that must be carried out, and no one can find mental fulfillment through it.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...You're right.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Look forward. Chew up and swallow your past, then make sure emptiness and bitterness are not the only flavors you know.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Remember that there is a whole world behind you waiting to be saved.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I will keep that in mind.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I have a final favor to ask: Please look after the Kremnoan warriors in my absence.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: They will undoubtedly face challenges while assimilating into Okhema... It is my sole regret that I cannot stand by them during this time.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Do not worry. Leave it to me.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: And while I'm at it, I'm going to find out if the Kremnoan language is really missing that many words.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph, the Kremnoan philosophy can never be encapsulated in a mere dictionary.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But... if there's a chance in the next life, you should come visit my library.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I'll be on my way, Deliverer. Remember to stay alive till the final act.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Same goes for you. Don't die too easily —
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: May triumph always be yours, Mydeimos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Oh, right.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: One last question.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Go ahead. You better not leave any regrets behind.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Are you the one who told Chartonus about the signet ring?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Well...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Who knows?

rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...You're right, Mydeimos.

rows.text: I once believed those words without question until your father cast you into the Sea of Souls.
rows.speaker: Gorgo, Mydei's Mother

rows.text: It was at that moment I realized how everything I believed in was utterly hollow. Perhaps the spirit of Kremnos had once existed... but as greed bloomed in the hearts of humanity over the years, such spirit had long faded alongside our glory.

rows.text: I no longer put my faith in any oath or doctrine. Now, I have just one role...

rows.text: ...That dream always ends there. The journey back to Castrum Kremnos is proving to be longer than expected.

rows.text: Yet each night, she would show up, waiting by the flickering firelight. I always anticipated the sequel to that dream, believing she had more words of wisdom or guidance to offer...

rows.text: Oh, I know! I'll turn the moon into a ship and the stars into sails to go find Mama! Pinky promise?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Mmm, pinky promise.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: As long as you sail toward tomorrow, as long as the sun will rise for the next day...
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: Our wishes will come true together.
rows.speaker: Gentle Mother

rows.text: This way. Now, we'll go through this shelf.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: But how? With {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}' power?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So, this obstacle... it was simply a mirage?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yes, the answer is right on the shelf. Go ahead and give it a try.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: It's a secret passage...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It was a secret passage prepared by the Holy Maiden's supporters for Mother and me as a precaution...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: And now, it has turned into our passage to escape, just as anticipated.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: I can't move it... Can't climb over it either...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Time Titan... is that you?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Just like this.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Regardless of our actions, the past will remain unchanged. It was someone else who helped Tribios in the actual events of history.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: We don't remember the details. As for why Memory recreated the past to be like this, it must be because...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: It's closer to the answer within our heart.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: The passage... is now cleared!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Thank you, nameless god!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: She's about to reveal the answer.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: But nothing happened.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What was making her, or you, hesitate at this moment?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If she had known this Flame-Chase Journey would proceed as the Titan foretold, bringing about great suffering and fatalities, including her own...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Would she still have chosen to walk through the gate and start her journey?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I think...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: The answer is already within you, and you've made your own decision.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: ...What?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You can... hear us?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not really...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: She can neither see nor hear us.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Yet, she knew that one day, someone would return to unveil this dust-covered memory.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: We can never know for sure who helped us back then. But that kindness was forever engraved in our hearts, motivating us to move forward. Time has modified this memory into a special letter, so that we do not forget our original intent.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: It's a letter written by Tribios of the past and sent to her future self. In this memory, it is Tribios of the future who overcomes all difficulties for her and sends her on a long journey... toward the tomorrow where we are.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Yes, you'll remember it all, and then find your way back to the gate where everything began.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Here, I will set sail toward the distant horizon.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Here, you have traveled far on your way home.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Such is the maxim that unveils Tribios' fate: "You shall shatter into a thousand fragments and wither on the soil of foreign lands."
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: So, if you ever feel lost, return to this place. I'll keep this memory here for you — or for me — to embrace it again.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Worry not. Though loss is something we've grown used to, our resolve and our pledge are what Tribios will never forget.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Each one of us has never failed to remember.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "Losses are a constant on the Flame-Chase journey, among which even life itself holds little value."
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "The hot blood of the sacrificial lamb will not be spilled in vain, like my mother and I."
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "The libations poured are guaranteed to bear fruit, just as my blade-wielding right hand is not a hollow formality."
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: "Surmount the myriad passages of {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}, and we will once again—"
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "Ride the west wind and let the wings carry us far away."
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: So this... is your answer.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's right. In the name of the Three Fates, I stand by my answer with no regrets.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Now, with or without the gods' blessing...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: I run towards the world's agony.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: If I can truly pierce through the utter darkness...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: We will meet again at the end of the west wind where flowers bloom in spring.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Light Calendar 3760, Month of Evernight
"Janusopolis' Holy Maiden" Tribios bore the Coreflame to quell the world's chaos and became a demigod of Janus.
She traversed the "Gate of Infinity," splitting into a thousand messengers to spread the divine prophecy across the land of Amphoreus.
After a century of arduous journeying...
Light Calendar 3870, Month of Freedom
Humanity's Flame-Chase Journey officially began.
Please stay clear.
rows.speaker: Holy City Guard

rows.text: Ah, Lady Maiden!
rows.speaker: Amiable Woman

rows.text: Tribios... what does that name actually mean?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "The one with three lives." Mother believed our birth was blessed by the Three Titans of Fate. She named us thus to express her gratitude.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Looking at how things have unfolded, fate might have had a role in it.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Finally... the {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#} Vault is right ahead.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: By the blood of the lamb and the strength of my blade-wielding right hand...
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: I am Tribios, the Listener, the announcer, and the witness of the prophecy —
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: — I, the Holy Maiden of Janusopolis, the walker of the infinite paths, have come forth to assume your {RUBY_B#Coreflame}duty{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Hehe...
rows.speaker: Janus

rows.text: The one who guides the world shall see their soul shattered into a thousand fragments, akin to glass crashing upon the ground...
rows.speaker: Janus

rows.text: Just as I wished. This journey promises to be a long one. With a thousand selves to accompany me, I'll never be lonely.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Though thou bearest the Coreflame, thou shalt be far from the glory of divinity. "Passages" are forever associated with dirt, and even a mere mortal's blade can imperil thy very existence...
rows.speaker: Janus

rows.text: No matter. My hands are not made for bearing arms, but my feet are destined to embark on a journey for the benefit of all.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Yet, the Flame-Chase is a journey of constant loss, among which even life itself holds little value....
rows.speaker: Janus

rows.text: Time decays the heart, the passages shatter the body, and the scales weigh the separation, until the end draws near...
rows.speaker: Janus

rows.text: The one who bears three lives... art thou truly prepared?
rows.speaker: Janus

rows.text: Without a doubt, Titan. Let the prophecy shatter me —
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: — so that I may open a myriad of paths for this imperiled world!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: It's opening up! Move aside and get ready —
rows.speaker: Strict Holy City Guard

rows.text: The Holy Maiden...?
rows.speaker: Scared Holy City Guard

rows.text: The path... is opening up for me.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: O {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}... protect me.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: The main path is likely well-guarded... What do I do?
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: Just as I thought... Inside!
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: There are guards here, too. Don't alert them.
rows.speaker: Tribios

rows.text: While history might be blurred by memories, seeing how the whole city is hunting her down, she clearly had no allies...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Lady Tribbie, do you still think...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That everything will be fine tomorrow?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yeah, that's what Trianne would say as well.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: With all due respect...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lady Tribbie, you know perfectly well... that see you tomorrow is nothing but a white lie.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I hope your toughness is not a mask hiding a lonely heart.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Cas, that's not a lie.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: See you tomorrow is the greatest prophecy in the world.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Prophecy...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Listen. In every corner of this land, every heartbeat carries a prayer for that prophecy to come true.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: It may be that only a few heroes will bring tomorrow to the new world, but the prophecy of leading everyone to tomorrow belongs to all in Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: But not everyone has the chance to see tomorrow. How can such words be called a prophecy?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Because people believe it will come true, and they are trying hard to hold onto that belief.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Even as the world teeters on the brink of collapse, everyone is pressing forward, longing to reach farther and move toward tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: And that is why a Holy Maiden exists to lead the world toward tomorrow, and why Janusopolis' prophecy unfolds as passages.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "Fate" is not about the outcome, but the journey. It's not the flowers that bloom at the end of the road...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: But rather the paths that lead beyond the gate, where people tread toward the sea of flowers.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: So, Cas, if anything is troubling you, just set it aside for tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: There's no difference between demigods and mortals. The troubles we encounter can only be resolved by our future selves.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Reflect through the long night, wait for the dawn as you think, then set off at daybreak. The hesitant part of us will be left behind in the dark, while the determined side of us will know no fear.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Because that's how Tribios has journeyed so far to spread the prophecy...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Beckoning the morning sun... and the tomorrow it promises to bring.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Hehe...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Child of humanity, surely you are not waiting for the arrival of night?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Nights do not fall upon Okhema.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That's why it's futile for you to wait here.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...Honestly, I didn't expect the renowned Reason Titan to behave like this.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh... And that's all thanks to you. If your soul weren't as prickly as a hedgehog, I wouldn't have to act this way.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: If you were more accommodating, you wouldn't be opposing me all the time, and I could teach you more freely instead.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: It was you who insisted on implanting the Coreflame in me... Forget it. Cut the sarcasm and just say what you need to say.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Fine, fine. All I want is to remind you...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: There's not much left in your soul. If you don't do something soon, I will have to take over this body.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: If I'm not worried, why should you be? I know what you're planning. You just want my help answering the question —
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: "What exactly are 'we'?" Correct?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It's good that you remember. Thus, "equivalent exchange" — it's only fair.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Then, rest easy. The answer will soon be revealed, and you'll have to return my body shortly.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hehe, is that true?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Certainly. I initially thought this extremely frail state would hinder me from getting my body back...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But I didn't expect the answer to be right within it. Hmph, that saved me a lot of trouble — I don't even need the black-robed swordmaster's ceremonial blade.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That's certainly worth celebrating.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Regrettably... I can't carry out the upcoming experiment alone.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The girl who's walking with death... is she fully prepared?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Be patient, Titan...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If we're always so guarded, how can "Death" reach us easily?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Unfortunately, on behalf of Okhema, I must ask you to slow your pace.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Heh... I forgot about you. My apologies.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: A child's words are always carefree. I'll just dismiss these words as nonsense from a cheeky child.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Come now, conceited "performer." It's time to address your relationship with {RUBY_B#Reason Titan, Cerces}that Titan{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: What if I refuse?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Provocation will only tip {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#}'s scales further toward your demise. There's no need to go to such lengths.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: O monster neither human nor divine, don't forget that you won't dare kill me. If you snuff out the Coreflame of "Reason" —
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What else can you use to stand against the Council?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Eh... Do you two mind if I cut in?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I warned you. Do not interrupt me —
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Ahh. I just have been meaning to ask: Does death really matter to you?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What I mean is, before I implanted the Coreflame into your heart...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...you were already a silent, cold corpse.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I'm back. Finally have a moment to catch my breath. Want to chat, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's unusual to see Mem isn't with you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Since they're not here, let me ask you — are you really sure you want to take on the trial of {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame on behalf of the Chrysos Heirs?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...We've ended up at this point after all. This is probably a fate that "Trailblaze" can't evade.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You should be extra cautious and watch out for yourself. Based on the experiences of those before you, the trial is no walk in the park.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But what concerns me even more is that you'll further bind yourself to Amphoreus... If you truly assume that Titan's divinity, do you believe you'll be able to lay it down again?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Forget it. We'll deal with that when the time comes. No matter what happens, I'll be right there with you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: They said they were messengers of the Council of Elders and wanted to verify my identity.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But I suspect we've been on their radar for a while... and they only made their move when you and I got separated.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Their questions were quite specific, from how we arrived in Okhema to our relationships with each Chrysos Heir. They even asked about what we did in the market.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Luckily, those pawns aren't the brightest. I managed to brush off most of their questions, so they'll probably leave us alone for a bit.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But on second thought, Aglaea also initially kept her guard up with us. It's best not to provoke either side until we know the full truth.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The only thing we know for sure is that some members of the Council of Elders aren't happy with the Chrysos Heirs. In the worst-case scenario... we could be caught up in the internal conflicts of the holy city.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If only we had more time to sort through the clues about the black tide. But now...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The weather is the only lovely thing left. Let's take some more pictures.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Huh? What's going on?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Something wrong, Dan Heng?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ah...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The memory card is full.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I bet March and the others are pretty worried too.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: And so, this long day passed for Okhema.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Some people arrived, and some left forever, just like every other day of this journey where we, stumbling, move forward.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We have long been prepared. If we are to chase the flames, then we must grow used to farewells. And yet...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: No one back then could foresee...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "Death"... Its arrival would always be so sudden and so momentous.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Even [Trailblazer], coming from beyond the sky, could not escape the Reaper's two hands. And what people gained and lost in that trial of "Death"...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Was far heavier than "Life" itself.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Just like the destiny that the prophecy revealed for Cas...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "At the end of the sea of flowers, the souls of the living shall warm thy fingertips..."
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: "And after an embrace... there shall be eternal separation."
rows.speaker: Tribbie
